description: Kazo OS platform core: app catalog, process manager, policy, shell, settings and logs as files, gateways behind the SDK. For composing an OS host.
releaseNotes:
Kazo OS 3.3.3, changes for app developers:
- Kazo.Os.AppSdk.Craft: the shared module of the Craft apps. A new SDK library shipped and served by Kazo OS for the apps that show a Craft app (Rust compiled to WebAssembly) in an iframe of their window: CraftFrame (the iframe and its messages), DocumentSession and SaveDecision (bound files, changes, title, close), CraftDocumentFormats, WebStorageFile (per-user settings in ~/.config/<appId>/), PickRequest, ReservedKeys and CraftLanguage. Taken from Kazo Word and made generic (ADR 0259).
- Opening a file no app supports names the Store apps that can open it. When no installed app opens a file, the OS looks in the Store catalogs it already downloaded for the apps that declare the file type, without waiting for the network. xdg-open lists them with the kazopkg install command, and KazoApps.OpenFileAsync returns them in KazoOpenFileResult.SuggestedCatalogApps.
- The File Explorer proposes Store apps for a file no app opens. Opening a file no installed app supports now shows the Open with box with the Store apps that declare its type: icon, name, short description and a View in the Store button. The Store opens on the app's page and, once the app is installed, opens the file. Open with shows the same section under the installed apps. Apps can ask for the list with KazoApps.GetSuggestedCatalogAppsAsync.
- App repositories show their Store listing in the README. The kazoos-solution template's README starts with the app's Kazo OS Store listing, a Try it section and a short presentation of Kazo OS. .github/scripts/store-readme.mjs copies the description, icon and screenshots of store/ into README.md and readme-fr.md, and CI fails when a README differs from store/.
- Kazo.Os.AppSdk.Craft reads GridCraft's documents and languages. OpenDocument.ListFrom now reads both shapes of ui.inspect (WordCraft's documents with ids, GridCraft's windows pointing at documents), with a new overload that names a document with no path from its title. CraftLanguage.Pick falls back to the two-letter code when the Craft app lists only those. The Craft app guide adds the pitfalls of the close guard and the missing window menu.
- Craft apps stay on their screen instead of losing their document. Sending a window to another screen reloaded the iframe of Craft apps such as Kazo Word, which lost the open document. A window can now declare window.canChangeScreen: false (WindowOptions.CanChangeScreen): it opens on screen 1, Other screen shows a greyed-out entry, and a screen shortcut or a drop on another screen shows a notification: known issue, a fix is in progress.
- Guide and end-to-end test for Craft apps on the Kazo.Os.AppSdk.Craft module. A new guide, framework/craft-apps.md, shows how to write a Craft app window on the module: the iframe page, the CraftFrame events, the save rule, the minimum OS version. build/publish-trimmed.sh now packs a Craft test package (a window around a fake Craft app), installs it with kazopkg in the trimmed OS and drives it: open, save, Save As through a reserved chord, changes, an error after ready, theme, file picker, close guard and per-user settings. The Craft app port guide is rewritten on the module.
- Shared scripts for the Craft apps' iframe. The Kazo.Os.AppSdk.Craft module serves craft-host.js (OS side) and craft-proxy.js (in the iframe, with its file picker, reserved shortcuts and settings modules), taken from Kazo Word. An app's iframe page names its app with data-craft-app and its build with data-craft-build; saves with an id get saved back, and errors after ready reach the window as error.
- The direct link logs the Store opened for an account, and is tested end to end. /var/log/apps/org.kazoos.app-link.log gets an app-link.store-opened line when an account signs in and the Store opens at the app's page. build/publish-trimmed.sh now runs three direct link journeys (no account, account, missing app and cancel) against the official catalog served locally and signed by a key created for the run.
Release notes: https://github.com/Kazo-ca/Os/releases/tag/v3.3.3
